content.comment_body: Hello everyone, apologies for my English and any misunderstandings. I am trying to read values from a [company_name] Countis E24 Ethernet Modbus counter using my [product_name]. The communications tables are available here: [url]. However, I cannot establish communication even though the PORT and address are entered correctly. I suspect the problem comes from the table, but I lack experience with this protocol and hope someone can assist me.
Could you upload your [product_name] program as a ZIP file?
Hello, thank you for your reply. This is a beta test program made simply to check if I can read a value from the [company_name] counter.
I do not have access to that address.

The Modbus holding register (50514) is a double register (50514 + 50515). You need to transfer two words starting at address 50514. There is an issue though: this value is a 32-bit unsigned integer, while the [product_name] can only read 32-bit or 64-bit float values using its F/I converter, not 32 or 64-bit unsigned integer values.

Example: Transfer two words from start address HR50514 to your [product_name], start address VW0, two words. If the value is less than 32,768, you can read the value in the right two bytes, which is VW2, with a standard analog network input. Are you certain the Modbus port is 505? And is the Unit-ID set to 255?

Thank you very much for taking the time to help. Here is a screenshot of the communication table. Regarding port and ID: The port is configurable on the [company_name] E24, and typically port 502 is set. The default ID is 255, but I will try 1. Concerning the tables, dealing with 32 bit is a problem as the sign can be misplaced on the BIT. I will read it using a specific software like Modbus Doctor to see if these correspond to the expected value.

You may need to use 50515 (+50516) as the start address if there is an offset of +1. Modbus servers commonly use port 502 by default, so it is surprising you set port 505 in the transfer table. I am not sure what unit ID your Modbus device uses as the documentation does not specify. What voltage are you measuring – is it 230VAC? If so, a simple analog network input should work. For 230 VAC, you would read 230.00, and analog inputs may go up to 327.67 VAC.

analysis.insight_summary: The core challenge is establishing MODBUS TCP/IP communication between the user's [product_name] and a third-party [company_name] Countis E24 Modbus counter, particularly when attempting to read 32-bit unsigned integer values from the counter. A technical limitation is identified: the [product_name] cannot directly read unsigned 32-bit integer values from the MODBUS registers, leading to interpretation issues for registers exceeding 16-bit. Discussions further delve into MODBUS specifics such as port numbers, unit IDs, and address offsets, compounding user confusion and communication problems.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects their [product_name] to reliably read all relevant register values, especially 32-bit unsigned integers, from the [company_name] counter via MODBUS, without requiring manual conversion or creating interpretation challenges.
